title: Cache index misalignment - deadlock runbook draft
content:
Summary:

This is a working runbook + incident review draft for the outage on 2026-03-08 that manifested as persistent request stalls and eventual OOMs on serving-runtime workers. We observed a rare cache-index misalignment between the in-memory KV index and the persisted eviction metadata which, combined with continuous-batching inflight requests, caused a lock acquisition deadlock that prevented background eviction and allowed the working set to grow until the process hit OOM.

Why this doc exists:
- Produce concise on-call steps to mitigate the failure quickly in future
- Capture root cause analysis and temporary mitigations already applied
- Track concrete action items (short-term and long-term) and owners

Impact:
- Affecting: ~12% of hosted inference requests in us-west-2 during the incident window.
- Symptoms: long tail latencies, stalled streaming responses, worker crash loops due to OOM.
- Customer visible: intermittent 504s and truncated streams for customers on dedicated and hosted tiers; no data leak or corruption of user payloads detected.

High-level timeline (abbreviated):
- 2026-03-08 02:04 UTC: Spike in request queue length and first SLO alerts.
- 02:06 UTC: Multiple workers reported >95% free memory consumed, background eviction not progressing.
- 02:09 UTC: First worker OOM; restart event created cascade of connection failures.
- 02:12 UTC: On-call (eng-sre pager) acknowledged; mitigation doc initiated.
- 02:20 UTC: Rolling restart of impacted worker pool to free memory; partial recovery but recurring within 40 minutes.
- 03:05 UTC: Engineering deep-dive: found stale reference counts and index entries in the KV cache; eviction thread blocked waiting on index lock held by continuous-batching path.
- 04:30 UTC: Temporary feature-flag rollout: disable concurrent eviction + hot-prefix prefetch in affected pools; stabilizes memory usage.

Observed signals and debug artifacts used:
- Heap profiles from crashed processes (captured with pprof) showing growth in kv-entry objects with refcount > 1 and non-zero size.
- Thread stacks showing eviction thread waiting on rwlock with cont-batcher holding write lock while executing batch fusion code.
- /metrics: eviction-rate dropped to 0 while cache-entries grew 3x for a hot-model shard.
- Application logs: repeated warnings about index-version-mismatch for keys in the hot partition.

Root cause (interim):
- Race in KV index update path: when a prefix prefetch inserted entries into the in-memory index, it sometimes wrote the index version header but failed to update the corresponding eviction metadata due to an early return path on transient network error with the metadata store. This left entries with a version mismatch.
- Continuous batching code path assumed index and eviction metadata were consistent and took a lock ordering that differs from the eviction thread (batching takes index lock then metadata lock; eviction takes metadata lock then index lock). Under a particular interleaving, this induced a circular wait -> deadlock between batching and eviction threads.
- Deadlock prevented eviction from reclaiming memory; continuous-batching kept inflight KV references alive which prevented GC of entries and caused resident set to grow until OOM.

Why this slipped through tests:
- The integration test suite did not exercise the particular failure mode: short network hiccup during prefetch combined with high QPS continuous-batching at a specific concurrency level.
- Locks ordering was locally documented but not enforced via linter/assertions. Unit tests mock cache store responses and did not simulate partial write failure semantics.

Immediate mitigations taken during incident:
1) Rollback/feature-flag: disabled hot-prefix prefetch and reduced continuous-batching concurrency to 1 on affected pools (rolled via infra feature flag). 
2) Rolling restart of workers to recover memory pressure and clear inconsistent in-memory state.
3) Added a temporary guard in the index update path: if metadata write fails, mark entry as ephemeral and avoid adding to main index until metadata confirmed. (This is a short-lived guard that is intended to be removed once the proper fix is merged.)
4) Escalation: paged runtime-team and applied coordinated deploy with monitoring in staging before prod rollout.

Proposed on-call runbook (draft):
Trigger: High eviction-age + falling eviction-rate paired with growing cache-entries and rising RSS (resident set) in serving-worker metrics, plus thread stacks showing index/metadata lock waits.

On-call steps (short checklist):
- Acknowledge pager and attach incident in SRE channel #sre-incident (tag: @oncall).
- Check metrics: /metrics -> eviction_rate, cache_entries_by_shard, worker_rss, continuous_batch_inflight.
- Obtain thread dump for at least one impacted worker: run curl http://worker:6060/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2 and save output. Look for patterns: eviction thread waiting on lock or batcher holding index write lock.
- If deadlock suspected: reduce continuous-batching concurrency via feature flag for the pool: FAAS_FLAG_CONT_BATCH_CONCURRENCY=<pool>=1.
- If eviction_rate == 0 and RSS > threshold: schedule rolling restart on the subset of instances in the pool (staggered, 30s drain, 2x parallel).
- If restart fails to reduce pressure: temporarily disable hot-prefix prefetch: FAAS_FLAG_PREFETCH_HOT_PREFIX=<pool>=off.
- Notify runtime-engineering and create incident ticket with collected artifacts (thread dump, pprof heap, metrics snapshot, relevant logs).

Safe observable checks after mitigation:
- eviction_rate returns to > 10 entries/s for impacted shards within 5 minutes
- cache_entries_by_shard declines to baseline within 15 minutes
- worker_rss decreases and stabilizes below memory alert threshold
- request latencies recover to normal percentiles

Post-incident action items (short-term, owners):
- (MC) Add a runtime assertion and a unit test to prevent lock-ordering inversion: ensure a single canonical lock acquisition order across prefetch, batching, and eviction paths. Due: 2026-03-19
- (PN) Harden index update path: make metadata writes transactional (or strongly consistent) with index updates; integrate retry/backoff to avoid early-returns that leave inconsistent state. Due: 2026-04-02
- (LO) Extend integration harness to simulate partial-metadata-store failures under high QPS continuous-batching. Add a long-running stress job in CI. Due: 2026-03-26
- (YP) Instrument and add alerting: new alert SRE-KV-LOCK-HOLDING if any eviction thread waits > 10s on index/metadata locks, and alert SRE-KV-ZERO-EVICTION if eviction_rate==0 for >30s and cache_entries increase >2x. Due: 2026-03-16
- (MC+Infra) Remove temporary guard (ephemeral mark) only after the transactional fix is merged and validated in canary. Expected: post 2026-04-02

Longer-term engineering roadmap items:
- Replace coarse-grained index locks with fine-grained per-shard locks to limit lock contention and reduce deadlock surface.
- Re-evaluate continuous-batching semantics: avoid holding index locks for the full duration of batch fusion; instead snapshot indices or use optimistic reads where safe.
- Persistent eviction metadata store: move to a strongly-consistent KV (or use a local write-ahead log) so index+metadata updates can be atomic.
- Chaos tests: include network partition and transient write failures against metadata store as part of weekly chaos runs.

Communication and customer notes:
- Customers impacted were notified via status.redwo od.com incident post (template in Confluence). No exposure of customer data.
- Customer Success (CS) owners: notify customers who saw >10% error rate in their integration for manual follow-up.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How often does index-version mismatch occur in other regions? We observed only us-west-2 in this incident; need to sweep logs for similar warnings elsewhere.
- Was there a correlated metadata-store throttle or GC event that precipitated the write error we saw? Need infra logs from metadata store cluster.

References / artifacts collected:
- Jira: SRE-1427 (incident ticket), RTE-889 (fix: transactional index/metadata update), RTE-890 (eviction + lock refactor).
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1854 (temporary guard), PR-1860 (lock-ordering assertion).
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/123456789/KV+Index+Deadlock+Postmortem (internal draft).
- Slack threads: #runtime-ops (link to message threads pinned in ticket).

Appendix: quick diagnostic commands for on-call
- curl "http://worker:6060/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2" > goroutines.txt
- curl "http://worker:6060/debug/pprof/heap?seconds=30" > heap.pb.gz (use pprof tool to inspect)
- kubectl logs -n serving-runtime deploy/worker-pool-P -c runtime --since=10m | grep -E "index-version|eviction|prefetch|OOM"
- query metrics (prometheus):
  - query: rate(kv_eviction_ops_total[1m])
  - query: kv_cache_entries{shard="hot-123"}

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally a working draft — please add comments inline in Confluence and signal any missing runbook steps. I want the on-call checklist to be executable by a new SRE on first page.

Document history:
- 2026-03-09: initial draft (MC)
- 2026-03-11: added on-call checklist and immediate mitigations (PN, LO)
- 2026-03-12: added action owner assignments and alerting suggestions (YP)

End of draft.
